Amanda, good morning. I am Anton Larin. I start today, and I am meeting every department this week.
Good morning. I am the legal manager here, so I look after the legal department.
Tell me what that means in practice. I am an economist, not a lawyer.
My team handles three kinds of matter: contracts, litigation and advisory work.
Start with the contracts. Who writes them?
We draft them here. I am the lawyer who reviews every contract before the commercial team signs it.
And litigation? Do you go to court yourself?
Not usually. We choose the firm that represents us in court, and my team controls the strategy.
One last question. What is not your responsibility?
Employment law. An outside firm takes care of that, and I deal with everything else.
I am the lawyer who reviews every contract.
We work for a group that exports grain to forty countries.

Hi Amanda, it's Irina from the group office. Quick one about next week. Anton Larin arrives on Monday as our new Group Operations Director for South America, and he wants to meet the head of every department before the end of the week. He has one afternoon for the whole site, so each manager gets three minutes. Three minutes, no slides. Please tell him three things: which matters your team handles, who you work with inside the company, and one thing that is not your responsibility. And send me two lines about that by Thursday at noon, so that I can put them in his file. One more thing. He is a finance person, not a lawyer, so please avoid the Latin. Thank you, Amanda. Talk to you on Thursday.

Hello, everyone. My name is Anton Larin and I start on Monday as Group Operations Director for South America. I am recording this because I cannot meet all of you in person this week. A short introduction. I am an economist, not a lawyer, and for the last six years I looked after the grain business in Eastern Europe, so the South American operation is completely new for me. In my first month I want to understand how each department really works, and I mean the daily work, not the organisation chart. So when we meet, please tell me three things: what your team handles every week, who depends on you, and one problem that comes back again and again. Three minutes each is enough. Thank you, and see you next week.

Say your role and the company you work for. Then name the three kinds of work your team handles. Then say who you work with inside the company. Then say who you report to. And finally, say one thing that is not your responsibility, and who takes care of it.
